title: Fix crash on closed generic structs from referenced assemblies

lines.text: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).

Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
Members of a type defined in a referenced assembly are reported by the project that defines that type, so an unattributed public member of such a type must be fixed in its defining project.

requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement.intent: A [MessagePackObject] type with a member whose type is a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly must build cleanly and still get a generated resolver.

functional.text: The generator does not throw when a member's type is a closed generic struct or record struct defined in a referenced assembly.
The analyzer does not throw for the same member types.
The compiling assembly gets its generated resolver, as it does when the generic type is declared in the same project.

nonFunctional.text: A failure of the generator or analyzer must not pass silently as a build warning that leaves the assembly without a resolver. (inferred)
Behaviour for generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same project does not change. (inferred)

expectedBehaviours: Building a project whose [MessagePackObject] type has a member typed as a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly (for example a ValueTuple-like or a custom generic struct in another project or package) finishes without the source generator throwing IndexOutOfRangeException.
The same holds when the referenced generic value type is a record struct.
No CS8785-style warning saying the generator failed shows up for these member types.

expectedBehaviours: Running the MessagePack analyzers on a [MessagePackObject] type whose member is a closed generic struct or record struct from a referenced assembly does not throw, and no AD0001 analyzer-exception warning is reported.
The analyzer reports only the diagnostics that apply. The member type alone produces no spurious MsgPack diagnostics.
expectedTests: An analyzer test with a metadata reference to an assembly that defines a generic struct expects no diagnostics and no analyzer exception for a [MessagePackObject] member of that closed generic type.

expectedBehaviours: The compiling assembly gets its generated resolver and a formatter for the [MessagePackObject] type, just as it does when the generic struct is declared in the same project.

expectedBehaviours: For these inputs the build output contains no warning saying the generator or analyzer threw an exception, so the assembly cannot quietly end up without a resolver.
If the generator cannot handle a member type, it says so with a meaningful diagnostic or a failed build. It does not silently skip resolver generation.
expectedTests: A test checks that the generator run result for the reproduction case has no exception and no generator-failure warnings, and that the generated resolver source is present.

story.what: TypeCollector now wraps the analyzer's report callback so that a diagnostic is only reported when its location is in source within the compilation being analyzed. Diagnostics with no location, or a location from metadata or another compilation, are dropped. Two diagnostic sites stop indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] directly. They now resolve a location that may be null, so members declared only in metadata no longer throw. The change also flips the nullable-annotation check in the MsgPack014 analyzer, adds three tests that reference a generic struct or record struct as a metadata-only assembly, and documents in README and in the MsgPack004 docs that diagnostics for such types come from the defining assembly.
story.why: MP-2283: a [MessagePackObject] type whose member is a closed generic struct or record struct from a referenced assembly crashed the generator and analyzer with IndexOutOfRangeException. TypeCollector indexed syntax references that metadata symbols do not have. The crash surfaced as AD0001/CS8785 warnings, and the assembly was left without its generated resolver.

findings.title: MsgPack014 nullable formatter check inverted, unrelated to requirement
findings.detail: The requirement does not ask for this change. The MsgPack014 query now collects IMessagePackFormatter<T> interfaces whose reference-type argument is Annotated (T?) instead of NotAnnotated (T). As a result, formatters that already implement IMessagePackFormatter<T?> get the warning 'Implement IMessagePackFormatter<T?> (with nullable annotation)'. Formatters that lack the annotation, which are the ones the diagnostic exists for, are no longer flagged. Every correctly written formatter in user code would raise a false warning, which breaks builds that treat warnings as errors. Existing MsgPack014 tests would also fail, and no test change covers this.

findings.title: Report filter also drops diagnostics with no location
findings.detail: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation forwards a diagnostic only when Location.IsInSource is true. A diagnostic created with a null location (Location.None) is therefore dropped as well, even when the problem is in the compiling project. Location.None is allowed for analyzers; only locations in syntax trees outside the compilation are not. Several TypeCollector diagnostics get their location from helpers that can return null, such as GetIdentifierLocation, GetParameterListLocation, identifier?.GetLocation() for MemberNeedsKey, and FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax(). Before this change, those diagnostics were still reported without a location. Now they are discarded. The generator path never reports diagnostics, so the user gets no message at all, and GetObjectInfo may return null and leave the type without a formatter. This is the silent failure N1 rules out. The filter should drop only diagnostics whose source tree is not part of the compilation, and keep Location.None.

findings.title: No check of generated formatter output or runtime round-trip
findings.detail: The new tests skip the generated-sources check and only assert that the resolver hint name is present. Nothing checks that the resolver registers a formatter for the closed generic struct (for example MyGenericStruct<int> or Item<int>), or that the formatter emitted for the metadata-defined generic definition is correct. No test round-trips an instance through the generated resolver. F3 expects the cross-assembly case to produce the same resolver and formatter as the same-project case, and that is not verified.

findings.title: No test for a generic class from a metadata reference
findings.detail: The fix in the field loop (FirstOrDefault instead of [0]) affects any generic type loaded from metadata, because compiler-generated backing fields of a metadata type are not reported as implicitly declared. That includes generic classes, not just structs. The existing Generics_Defined_In_ReferencedProject test uses a project reference, so the type is source-backed. The new tests cover only structs and record structs from a compiled image. N2 says behaviour for generic classes must stay the same, and no test exercises a generic class from a metadata-only reference.
